In [[mathematics]], the '''Humbert polynomials''' π{{su|b=''n'',''m''|p=λ}}(''x'') are a generalization of [[Pincherle polynomials]] introduced by Pierre Humbert<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Humbert |first=Pierre |date=February 1920 |title=Some Extensions of Pincherle's Polynomials |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/product/identifier/S0013091500035756/type/journal_article |journal=Proceedings of the Edinburgh Mathematical Society |language=en |volume=39 |pages=21–24 |doi=10.1017/S0013091500035756 |issn=0013-0915}}</ref> given by the [[generating function]]

:<math>\displaystyle (1-mxt+t^m)^{-\lambda}=\sum^\infty
_{n=0}\pi^\lambda_{n,m}(x)t^n</math>

<ref>{{Citation |last1=Boas |first1=Ralph P. |chapter=Polynomial expansions of analytic functions |title=Ergebnisse der Mathematik und Ihrer Grenzgebiete |volume=19 |pages=58 |year=1958 |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=eihMuwkh4DsC |series=Neue Folge |location=Berlin, New York |publisher=[[Springer-Verlag]] |isbn=978-0-387-03123-1 |mr=0094466 |last2=Buck |first2=R. Creighton}}</ref>
